desc: Formalize the greedy expansion: prove that absorbing any strictly-smaller neighbor whenever possible yields a unique maximal final segment and size for each K. (Confluence/monotonicity established; final segment is the unique fixed point of the expansion.)

Implement rightward expansion table R[i] (furthest right reachable starting at i with only rightward moves) using a monotonic stack with prefix sums in O(N). (Design finalized: sweep right-to-left, stack of (threshold=A_j, block_sum, block_end), pop while threshold < current sum; verified on sample 1.)
Implement leftward expansion table L[i] symmetrically in O(N). (Sweep left-to-right with mirrored stack; verified on sample 1.)

Combine: for each K, alternate/merge left and right reachability. (Resolved: per-K alternating jump simulation using lend/rend + prefix sums; jump validity by monotonicity/replication argument; iteration count bounded by O(log Amax) per side via doubling of stop values; verified against sample 1 outputs 4 30 2 13 2 13 and spot-checked sample 2.)

Write final Python code: fast input parsing (sys.stdin.buffer), build P, lend, rend arrays, per-K simulation loop, print answers space-separated; keep inner loops tight (bind lists to locals, while-loops) to handle worst-case ~3e7 iterations.

Verify the submitted code against both samples and edge cases (strict `<`, endpoints, N=2, adversarial doubling chains), and tighten the hot loop if needed. (Both samples fully reproduced by hand-trace; strict-inequality boundaries, endpoint guards, N=2, and prefix-sum indexing all confirmed; hot loop already uses parallel-list stacks and localized bindings — no changes needed.)
